verses.1: Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
verses.2: They said, “Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has He not also spoken through us?” And the LORD heard it.
verses.3: Now the man Moses was very humble—more than any other human who had ever lived on the face of the earth.
verses.4: Suddenly the LORD spoke to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “All three of you come out to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three of them went out.
verses.5: The LORD descended in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tent, and He called, “Aaron and Miriam.” So the two of them came forward.
verses.6: He said, “Listen to My words: if there is among you a prophet of the LORD, I will reveal Myself to him in a vision, and I will speak with him in a dream.
verses.7: But not so with My servant Moses. He is faithful in all My house.
verses.8: I speak with him face to face, clearly, not in riddles, and he sees the form of the LORD. Why then did you not fear to speak against My servant, against Moses?”
verses.9: The anger of the LORD burned against them, and He left.
verses.10: The cloud lifted from above the Tent, and when Miriam came out, she was struck with leprosy—her skin as white as snow. Aaron turned to Miriam and saw that she had become leprous.
verses.11: Then Aaron said to Moses, “My lord, please do not let this sin be on us, for we have acted foolishly and sinned.”
verses.12: “Do not let her become as one dead, as if he were torn from the womb and half his flesh eaten.”
verses.13: Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her now.”
verses.14: The LORD said to Moses, “If her father had spit in her face, would she not be shamed for seven days? Let her be shut out for seven days, outside the camp, and after that she may be brought back in.”
verses.15: So Miriam was shut out from the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until Miriam was brought back in.
verses.16: Then the people departed from Chatzeros and camped in the Desert of Paran.

notes:
Notes
- v. 12: “as if he were torn from the womb and half his flesh eaten” — the Hebrew is ambiguous and metaphorical; the reference to the womb and half-eaten flesh may be idiomatic for a newborn or a corpse. The rendering follows the most natural interpretation of a leper as one who appears nearly dead.
- v. 14: “If her father had spit in her face” — the Hebrew uses a metaphor comparing divine judgment to the shame of being spat upon by a father. The translation preserves the metaphor without adding interpretation.
- v. 14: “would she not be shamed for seven days?” — the Hebrew implies a rhetorical question, so “would she not” is used to retain the tone.
